decision: Keep Three.js as the only scene renderer and Vue as the only DOM UI owner
reason: The repo already has a fixed-timestep Three.js engine, GLB assets, and Vue components; the references require a live 3D world plus accessible dialogue and settings.
tradeoff: The current imperative scene code keeps more lifecycle responsibility in the game layer, but avoids a migration and preserves the existing asset pipeline.

decision: Use lantern amber and leaf green as rare interface accents over parchment neutrals
reason: The references repeatedly use sunset amber, green foliage, pale paper panels, and dark ink; the palette ties UI to the world without adding a second visual language.
tradeoff: The muted palette has less immediate contrast than a neon HUD, so every live-scene label needs a backing surface and contrast check.

decision: Anchor the menu left and keep the world visible on the right
reason: The main-menu reference uses the open village and seated characters as the emotional hook; the menu should not cover the strongest scene composition.
tradeoff: A left anchor gives less room on narrow screens, so the responsive layout must collapse into a centered sheet below the mobile breakpoint.

decision: Use DOM dialogue and HUD rather than canvas text
reason: The s4 reference depends on readable captions, and DOM text provides keyboard focus, screen-reader access, responsive wrapping, and predictable contrast over the 3D scene.
tradeoff: The dialogue is screen-space rather than fully diegetic, but it remains readable at every camera distance and device size.

decision: Treat inventory as a spatial field kit and settings as a sequential list
reason: The invent reference places items in a grid while settings are organized as labeled rows; each screen gets the native metaphor instead of a generic card layout.
tradeoff: Two layouts require more component-specific CSS, but they reduce cognitive load and match the reference hierarchy.

decision: Keep the simulation fixed at 60Hz and cap rendering through the existing quality presets
reason: The project is a realtime 3D game and the reference world contains many vegetation meshes; stable movement and honest frame budgets matter more than post-processing.
tradeoff: The look will remain material-and-light driven rather than cinematic, but it is easier to sustain on lower-end devices and easier to debug.
